description:
Castello Dal Pozzo traces its origins to a Roman castrum built by the Fifth Legion on these hills above Lake Maggiore. Around the year 1000, the Visconti — a noble Milanese family — erected the first medieval fortress on the site. After a long period of decline, the Visconti d'Aragona restored the castle's remains in the 16th century, converting it into an elegant noble residence befitting the family's status.

In the 19th century, Marquis Claudio Dal Pozzo d'Annone commissioned British architect Richard Popplewell Pullan to redesign the complex in the Neo-Gothic Revival style, giving the estate its present striking silhouette above the lake. The estate today comprises three distinct architectural units built at different periods: the Neo-Gothic Castle itself, the 18th-century Visconti Palazzo, and the former Scuderie (stables) — together forming the 45-46 room Castello Dal Pozzo Resort, part of Preferred Hotels & Resorts.

The Roman-era castrum beneath the medieval fortress points to a strategic use of this hilltop above Lake Maggiore stretching back roughly two millennia, long before the Visconti family's involvement gave the site its documented medieval identity.

Richard Popplewell Pullan's involvement connects Castello Dal Pozzo to the wider 19th-century European fashion for Neo-Gothic Revival architecture, in which British architects were frequently commissioned by continental noble families seeking to give older structures a fashionable romantic silhouette.

The estate's division across three genuinely distinct buildings — rather than a single restored castle — reflects the gradual, centuries-long growth of a working noble estate, where new functions (a grander residence, working stables) were added as separate structures rather than folded into the original fortress.

Lake Maggiore's Borromean Islands and the town of Stresa, both a short drive away, give guests staying at Castello Dal Pozzo easy access to one of Northern Italy's most celebrated lake landscapes.

faqs.question: Are all the rooms at Castello Dal Pozzo within the castle itself?
faqs.answer: No — the 45-46 rooms are spread across three genuinely distinct historic buildings: the Neo-Gothic Castle, the 18th-century Visconti Palazzo, and the former Scuderie (stables). Ask at booking if staying within the Castle building specifically matters to you.

faqs.question: Who redesigned Castello Dal Pozzo in the 19th century?
faqs.answer: British architect Richard Popplewell Pullan, commissioned by Marquis Claudio Dal Pozzo d'Annone to redesign the complex in the Neo-Gothic Revival style.

faqs.question: Can I visit Castello Dal Pozzo without staying overnight?
faqs.answer: No confirmed independent day-visit product was found; it functions as a private resort hotel, part of Preferred Hotels & Resorts.

hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** About 15 minutes by car from Malpensa Airport; roughly 30 minutes from Stresa and the Borromean Islands on Lake Maggiore.

**Rooms & rates:** 45-46 rooms spread across three distinct historic buildings — the Neo-Gothic Castle, the 18th-century Visconti Palazzo, and the former Scuderie (stables). From €91/night.

**On-site:** Restaurant, gardens with lake views, event spaces.

**Good to know:** Which of the three buildings a room is in significantly affects the character of the stay — specify a preference at booking if staying inside the Castle itself matters to you, as opposed to the Palazzo or the former stables.

**Combine with:** Stresa and the Borromean Islands on Lake Maggiore, a short drive away.
